## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill (N≈949) lies below the smallest measured point, so its effect is invisible. At q=0.01, cost FALLS from 8.753 ns/p at N=4000 to 7.985 at N=65000 — overhead amortization, not a cache effect. Crossing the L2 spill (N≈60787) between N=4000 and N=65000 produces no knee: cost stays FLAT at ~8.0 ns/p through N=4M (8.016). Raising death rate lifts the floor without reshaping the curve: q=0.05 settles at ~8.3–8.8 ns/p, q=0.25 at ~10.2 ns/p, all flat across N≥65000. The N-shape is death-rate-invariant; only the floor moves.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.67 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 34% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.25 the peak falls to 6.77 GB/s (27%). The algo is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: it never approaches the streaming ceiling at any N or death rate. The transition is by death rate, not by N — bandwidth is flat across N within each q tier, confirming the bottleneck is per-particle compute/branch cost, not memory traffic.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the particle update. The hot loop (0x100055460+) uses scalar `ldp s5, s6`, `ldr s17`, `fadd s5`, `fmul s5`, `fcvtzs` — all `.s` (single-element) operations, one particle at a time. Zero vector-suffixed instructions appear in the histogram. The only SIMD is in the respawn-scan path: `ldp q1, q0` and `orr.16b v0, v1` batch-check 32 death-flag bytes, but this is a mask over the flag array, not component-wise vectorization. The scatter writes are byte-granular (`ldrb w2, [x1]` / `strb w2, [x1]` / `strb w11, [x23, x0]`), and 37 `bl` calls to `spawn` introduce branchy control flow. No gather (`ld1.s {vN}[i]`) is present. The scalar codegen and byte-stores explain why bandwidth stalls at 34% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — achieved bandwidth never exceeds 8.67 GB/s (34% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) because the compiler emitted zero vector instructions in the hot loop, processing particles with scalar `.s` ops and byte-granular `strb` scatter stores. The branchy respawn path (37 `bl` calls) further depresses throughput to 6.77 GB/s at q=0.25. Auto-vectorization did not materialize, so the streaming ceiling was never approached at any death rate.
